purpose: ARYANZZ V1 Full Release ownership map for workspace UI, styles, scripts, and tool modules.
rules: Edit only the workspace module that owns the requested page or feature.
Keep CSS selectors rooted under the workspace root; do not add broad body, html, or generic panel overrides to page modules.
Keep downloader/provider logic separate from Home layout, Profile UI, Owner UI, and navigation.
Shared navigation may change visibility and route state only; it must not rewrite downloader, profile, owner, or library feature data.
Auth UI, auth API, and security controls are owned by Auth and Security modules. Profile, Owner, Tools, Library, and Downloader must not edit auth assets or authentication storage.

features: tool category filters and live category counts
consistent back navigation for every tool screen
unified responsive visual system for all internal tool panels

sharedLayout.purpose: One-time DOM ownership and legacy-layout normalization only; no downloader, profile, owner or library feature logic.

featureModules.purpose: Media link analysis and download engine
Home platform picker and title search only
Create WhatsApp-style chat mockups for Android and iPhone and export PNG locally.
Searchable, responsive tutorials for all 21 tools, contextual help launchers, and locally saved learning progress.

Modular lightweight tools including Scam Evidence Analyzer: local OCR-assisted screenshot/chat review, phone and account extraction, URL risk heuristics, file metadata and EXIF GPS evidence, coordinate mapping, timeline, IndexedDB-local case storage and report export. Online checks open official portals manually; evidence is never uploaded automatically.

release.updatePolicy: Keep the public release label fixed at V1. Internal build identifiers may advance only for cache invalidation, deployment verification, and recovery checkpoints.
release.architecture: One release with independently owned feature modules. Do not flatten unrelated feature logic into a single handler or stylesheet.

architectureGuard.policy: Changes must stay within the owning module. Shared shell changes require an explicit cross-module reason and regression coverage.
